thread:
Leo: Heads up — we're seeing a p99 spike on /v1/generate for a handful of tenants since ~09:38 UTC. p95 is fine, p99 jumped from ~120ms -> ~3.8s. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/prod/requests?range=15m :eyes:
Anya: Thanks. Any correlated errors or just latency?
monitoring-bot: Alert: high_p99_latency detected for service=runtime route=/v1/generate region=us-west-2 at 2026-03-17T09:39:12Z (p99=3800ms)
Maria: I see a traffic shift to model variant redwood-large-quant on many hosts in us-west-2 around 09:30 (canary rollout window). Could be perf regression in that build.
Sam: Can we short-circuit: 1) apply a circuit-breaker on that model variant, 2) route a % of traffic to redwood-medium-q4, and 3) throttle any single tenant > 10 qps? Quick guardrails.
Jordan: I'll notify account team for the affected tenants. Should we also open a support escalation for the enterprise customers?
Anya: Need logs from the runtime hosts. Leo — can you paste the top slow traces?
Leo: quick trace dump (root span ids):
```
span: 0x7f8a2c - model_infer - 2026-03-17T09:37:58Z - 3.4s
span: 0x7f8a7d - attention_kv_cache - 2026-03-17T09:37:58Z - 2.9s
host: runtime-uw2-12
```
Sam: That KV cache path looks suspect. For mitigation I propose routing policy change via admin API (examples below).
Sam: Example command to add fallback route (run from ops jump):
```
curl -X POST https://admin.redwood.internal/v1/routing/update \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \n  -d '{"match":{"model":"redwood-large-quant","region":"us-west-2"},"action":{"fallback":"redwood-medium-q4","pct":70}}'
```
ops-bot: @Sam — running routing change now (ticket 8742).
ops-bot: Applied circuit-breaker: model=redwood-large-quant threshold=1500ms window=60s action=failfast
Anya: Routing rule applied and CB enabled at 09:49 UTC. Shifted ~68% of traffic to redwood-medium-q4.
monitoring-bot: Alert resolved: high_p99_latency for route=/v1/generate region=us-west-2 at 2026-03-17T09:51:02Z (p99=310ms) :tada:
Maria: Nice. p99 dropped back under 400ms after fallback. Need follow-ups: 1) rollback the canary for redwood-large-quant, 2) add an automated fallback policy for future rollouts, 3) create short-term SLO guardrail (per-model p99 threshold) in the router config, and 4) add tenant-level soft-rate-limits to protect system from noisy customers.
Jordan: I'll draft the customer-facing note and get the account owner looped in.
Sam: For the SLO guardrail RFC (short): propose config keys: `model_p99_threshold_ms`, `cb_latency_window_s`, `fallback_model`, `fallback_pct`, `tenant_qps_cap`. We should enforce at the router control-plane and surface overrides per-enterprise.
Anya: Also add a quick synthetic test: small-sequence infer on redwood-large-quant in staging to catch regressions in kv-cache path.
Leo: Action items: 
- Jordan: notify affected customers + support ticket (ETA 30m)
- Sam: prepare rollback + reproduction plan for redwood-large-quant (ETA 1h)
- Maria: update router config to include automatic fallback + p99 guardrail (ETA 2h)
- Anya: collect runtime traces and KV cache metrics, attach to the incident (ETA 45m)
I will close this thread once ticket + short-term mitigations are in place. :thumbsup:
Maria: Filing postmortem checklist item and scheduling a quick post-incident sync.
Leo: Thanks everyone. Closing thread — mitigation worked, follow-ups assigned.
